---
title: "Results: Dual-Target Multiplex Compatibility"
---

To enable simultaneous point-of-care detection of **Influenza A** and **Influenza B** in a single reaction tube, candidate assays designed for the Indonesian cohort were evaluated using the **Multiplex Compatibility Screening Engine** (`scripts/m11_multiplex_checker.py`).

The screening engine evaluates all pairwise heterodimerization thermodynamics ($\Delta G$), kinetic melting temperature alignment ($\Delta T_m$), and fluorophore channel separation across a 6-oligo reaction mixture ($\text{Fwd}_A, \text{Rev}_A, \text{Probe}_A, \text{Fwd}_B, \text{Rev}_B, \text{Probe}_B$).

---

## 1. Dual-Temperature Screening Regimes

To guarantee assay robustness, the top Influenza A MP and Influenza B MP candidates were paired across their leading ranks and screened; **15 combinations survived the pre-pairing selection gates** and were evaluated across two temperature regimes:

1.  **Isothermal RT-RAA Mode ($39.0^\circ\text{C}$)**: Primary operational temperature for point-of-care recombinase-mediated amplification.
2.  **qPCR Comparative Benchmark ($55.0^\circ\text{C}$)**: Gold-standard laboratory thermal cycling benchmark.

---

## 2. Top Recommended Multiplex Assay Combinations

The table below highlights the top 5 multiplex combinations ranked by candidate selection gates (combining coverage, specificity, and multiplex compatibility scores), accounting for cross-dimer penalties, 3'-end anchoring, and kinetic alignment:

| Rank | Candidate Pair | Compatibility Score | RAA ΔG (39°C) | 3' Anchor | qPCR ΔG (55°C) | ΔTm (°C) | Status (39°C) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`FluA_Rank10_x_FluB_Rank12`** | **64.5** | **-7.19 kcal/mol** | **5 bp** | **-3.49 kcal/mol** | **2.23°C** | <span style="color: #10b981; font-weight: bold;">PASS</span> |
| **2** | **`FluA_Rank1_x_FluB_Rank12`** | **64.0** | **-7.19 kcal/mol** | **5 bp** | **-3.49 kcal/mol** | **2.42°C** | <span style="color: #10b981; font-weight: bold;">PASS</span> |
| **3** | **`FluA_Rank4_x_FluB_Rank12`** | **66.5** | **-7.19 kcal/mol** | **5 bp** | **-3.49 kcal/mol** | **1.59°C** | <span style="color: #10b981; font-weight: bold;">PASS</span> |
| **4** | **`FluA_Rank4_x_FluB_Rank8`** | **66.3** | **-7.19 kcal/mol** | **5 bp** | **-3.89 kcal/mol** | **1.63°C** | <span style="color: #10b981; font-weight: bold;">PASS</span> |
| **5** | **`FluA_Rank10_x_FluB_Rank8`** | **64.4** | **-7.19 kcal/mol** | **5 bp** | **-3.89 kcal/mol** | **2.27°C** | <span style="color: #10b981; font-weight: bold;">PASS</span> |

### Key Biophysical Observations:
*   **Zero Veto Violations**: All top combinations exhibit a worst-case cross-dimer binding energy $\Delta G > -12.0\text{ kcal/mol}$ (worst observed $\Delta G = -7.19\text{ kcal/mol}$), preventing spontaneous primer-dimer formation or competition during strand exchange.
*   **3'-End Safety**: All 3' complementarity runs remain $\le 5\text{ bp}$, well below the threshold for priming non-specific noise.
*   **Kinetic Balance**: $T_m$ differences across all primers in the multiplex mixture stay within acceptable bounds for isothermal and thermal cycling regimes.
*   **Fluorophore Independence**: Influenza A probe uses FAM ($\lambda_{\text{em}} = 520\text{ nm}$) and Influenza B probe uses HEX ($\lambda_{\text{em}} = 556\text{ nm}$), eliminating optical crosstalk.

## 3. Oligo Synthesis Specifications (Rank 1 Recommended Pair: `FluA_Rank10_x_FluB_Rank12`)

To ensure full transparency and laboratory synthesis readiness, the complete sequence strings, lengths, melting temperatures ($T_m$), GC percentages, and fluorophore dye modifications for all 6 oligos in the primary recommended multiplex set are listed below. The **primers** are shown as their **IUPAC-degenerate** sequences (e.g. `R` = A/G); the **probe** is shown as its **labeled order sequence** — the single majority-base sequence actually synthesised, carrying the internal FAM/HEX-dT, THF abasic site and BHQ1-dT quencher plus the 3′-C3 spacer. (The probe's degenerate form, with the `R`/`Y` positions, is listed on the [Candidate Diagnostics](results_candidates.qmd) page.)

### 🟩 Target A: Influenza A MP (FAM Channel)

| Oligo Name | Type | Sequence (5' $\rightarrow$ 3') | Length | Tm (°C) | GC (%) | Modification / Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **FluA_Fwd** | Forward Primer | `TCTGACTAARGGRATTTTRGGRTTTGTATTC` | 31 nt | 61.8°C | 35.5% | Unlabeled |
| **FluA_Rev** | Reverse Primer | `GCAGTTAAACTATATARGAARCTGAARAGRG` | 31 nt | 60.6°C | 35.5% | Unlabeled |
| **FluA_Probe** | Exo-Probe | `CCGTGCCCAGTGAGCGAGGACTGCAGCGTAGACGC[FAM-dT][THF][BHQ1-dT]GTCCAAAATGCCCT[C3-spacer]` | 51 nt | 82.3°C | 61.8% | Internal `FAM-dT`/`THF`/`BHQ1-dT` sandwich, `3'-C3-spacer` |

| Oligo Name | Type | Sequence (5' $\rightarrow$ 3') | Length | Tm (°C) | GC (%) | Modification / Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 5. N-Plex Capability

The multiplex engine is **N-plex capable** — it filters and computes cross-dimer thermodynamics for any requested target subset. This release targets the **Influenza A + Influenza B duplex only** (§1–§4 above), matching the project's scope of the Orthomyxoviridae family. Because the engine is generic, extending it to a further target requires only a new per-target build config — no change to the multiplex logic.
